proof_summary: Normalize \(T_n\) to \(u_n=T_n/2^{\lfloor\log_2T_n\rfloor}\in[1,2)\), so the bit is determined by whether \(u_n\) is below or above \(3/2\); the recurrence gives \(1.836\le T_{n+1}/T_n\le1.842\), hence each normalized step either multiplies by this ratio or by half of it. Threshold-crossing and repeated-contraction estimates then force at least four but at most five steps below \(3/2\), and at least three but at most four above it, with the finitely many initial cases handled directly.
